subject: AWS Private Offer — pilot term options and buyer approval choreography for GlobalPilot
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <procurement@globalpilot.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: m.ortega@globalpilot.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer — pilot vs scale term / approvals

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. We’re evaluating Redwood for a pilot in our Retail division (GlobalPilot Retail) with potential cross-division expansion if the pilot meets our latency and cost KPIs. A few things we need clarified to scope internal approvals and timeline: 

- Typical term length you recommend for a pilot that will convert to a larger commit (9/12/24 months?)
- How discounts or committed tiers are expressed in the AWS private offer (can we stage pricing so pilot gets a small credit and scale gets larger discounts?)
- Which buyer roles at our side need to sign in AWS Marketplace for a private offer to be fully approved (procurement vs. finance vs. legal)?
- Any docs you require from us to move to private offer (PO template, company creds, SOC2 evidence)?

We’d like to get an internal estimate of approval time so we can line up our kickoff date. Attaching our PO template for reference.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement — GlobalPilot Inc.
procurement@globalpilot.com

Attachment: GlobalPilot_PO_template.docx (docx)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <procurement@globalpilot.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — pilot vs scale term / approvals

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, then a recommended path below.

- Pilot term: we commonly do 3, 6, or 12 months; for pilots that must show measurable usage and metrics to internal stakeholders, 6 or 9 months is pragmatic.
- Pricing staging: yes — private offers can include tiered pricing and a staged discount schedule. We usually create a PO for the pilot with a small discount (or consumption cap) and a second, longer-term private offer or amendment for scale with a stepped discount.
- Buyer approvals: in most AWS Marketplace customers we’ve seen procurement + finance sign the private offer; legal typically reviews off-band. If your procurement system requires an internal PO + AWS signature, we can accommodate both.
- Docs: your PO template is fine; we’ll also want a primary contact, billing entity, and confirmation of who can sign in AWS Marketplace. SOC2 is helpful but not always required for the private offer transaction; if you need us to surface SOC2 reports we can provide a read-only link.

I’ve attached our vendor terms and a short buyer approval checklist. Vivek and Neha are looped for the recommended pricing/term structure and to confirm any platform constraints. Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to draft the mutual action plan?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: vendor_terms_v1.pdf (pdf), buyer_approval_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — pricing & term suggestion (internal)

FW: Internal notes — pricing suggestion for GlobalPilot: 

- Pilot offer: 6 months, committed $60k USD (effective blended price). Offer a pilot credit of $10k applied on invoice if KPIs met. This reduces procurement friction while keeping runway short.
- Conversion offer: 24 months, tiered usage bands: 0-500k tokens at $X, 500k-2M at $Y (20% off pilot blended), >2M at $Z (30% off pilot).
- Approval gating: procurement signs private offer in marketplace to enable vendor billing; finance must approve budget/commit internally; legal to review terms if duration > 12 months or if indemnities are modified.
- Timeline: if buyer has procurement + finance lined up, AWS private offer execution takes ~5–10 business days (create private offer, buyer review in marketplace, buyer acceptance). If legal redlines, add another 5–10 days.

I also recommend we pre-author the amendment that converts pilot to scale (pre-drafted DocuSign) to avoid delays.

— Vivek
Director, GTM — Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <procurement@globalpilot.com>
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: AWS private offer — pilot vs scale term / approvals

Hi Samantha — following up with a concise mutual action plan and next steps so your internal approvers see the routing clearly: 

1) Redwood sends: draft private offer (pilot: 6 months, $60k) + vendor terms + pre-drafted amendment to convert to 24-month scale. (We can keep the pilot discount conservative — $10k credit at success.)
2) GlobalPilot procurement: uploads PO to AWS Marketplace and routes to internal finance for budget sign-off (we will also accept PO directly to vendor billing if needed).
3) GlobalPilot finance: confirms budget and approves payment method (credit card vs. marketplace billing).
4) Procurement: accepts private offer in AWS Marketplace UI (this is the action that allows Redwood to invoice under the private offer).
5) Legal: optional review; will sign amendment for scale as needed.

Estimated calendar: if procurement + finance are ready, 7–10 business days from draft private offer to acceptance. With legal review, expect 12–20 business days.

I’ve uploaded a HubSpot deal for tracking and added links to the DocuSign amendment draft here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/GP-2026-009 — and will send a DocuSign envelope once we confirm pilot terms.

Would you be available Wed 26 Aug 10:00 PT for a 30-minute sync to finalize the pilot parameters?

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
